messages:
PagerBot: ALERT: Dedicated VPC pool for customer meridian-labs - canary allocation 7 shows sustained error-rate spike and large tail latency. Paging oncall. (svc=dedicated-inference, pool=dl-meridian-canary)
Ben (oncall): Acknowledge. Pulling logs now. Any known deploys in this pool in the last 30m?
Carla SRE: I see a new artifact rolled to canary ~12m ago: model-serving:2026-03-15-v1.3.7 (was v1.3.6). Error budget burn started ~8m after deploy, 5xxs and 504s for streaming endpoints.
Dmitri (eng-platform): Confirmed. Metrics: p50 latency up 2.1x, p95 up 4.6x, 5xx rate 6.3% sustained. Canary serving instances show repeated KV cache eviction logs.
Ben (oncall): Is this specific to meridian-labs or affecting other tenants in same pool?
Carla SRE: So far limited to tenants pinned to the canary artifact; some shared-traffic tenants routed to fallback model are fine. meridian-labs traffic is pinned to the canary via rollout policy.
Eva (CS): Meridian has live inference traffic (clinical triage). They're seeing timeouts reported by their app. They want a mitigation asap. I'm standing by to craft customer message once we have plan.
Fred (AM): I'll prep customer comms: 'We are investigating increased latency and errors impacting your calls. We'll update in 15 mins.'
Ben (oncall): Proposed mitigation: pin the meridian-labs tenant back to previous artifact (v1.3.6) and divert canary traffic. Rollback of canary globally is higher blast radius; prefer tenant surgical pinback + tenant isolation if needed. Thoughts?
Dmitri (eng-platform): Agree. We have a config knob: per-tenant pinned_artifact. We can set for meridian-labs and trigger a graceful reroute. Command: `redwoodctl tenant set-pin --tenant meridian-labs --artifact model-serving:2026-03-15-v1.3.6 --reason "canary regressions"`
Carla SRE: Also recommend isolating meridian-labs from the canary pool to stop ongoing stateful cache churn: `redwoodctl tenant isolate --tenant meridian-labs --pool dl-meridian-canary` Then move traffic to reserved-reserve-12.
Ben (oncall): I'm going to perform the pin first. Will run in prod and watch. If errors persist, we isolate.
DeployBot: ACTION STARTED by Ben (oncall): running `redwoodctl tenant set-pin --tenant meridian-labs --artifact model-serving:2026-03-15-v1.3.6`
DeployBot: ACTION SUCCESS: pin applied. Routing change propagated to edge proxies.
Carla SRE: Seeing immediate drop in 5xxs from meridian-labs, p95 dropping toward baseline. Nice.
Ben (oncall): Monitoring... p95 trending down. I still see a handful of 504s but much less.
Eva (CS): Sending customer note: "We applied a temporary pin to your inference artifact to restore stability. We're continuing to monitor and will follow up with root cause and ETA for a safe canary re-deploy." Want me to include any ETA?
Fred (AM): Keep it 'under investigation', we don't want to promise a time yet.
Dmitri (eng-platform): I'll start a deeper investigation into the artifact differences and KV cache behavior. Initial hypothesis: a kernel-level change in v1.3.7 modified memory allocation pattern causing eviction storms under long-seq workloads. I'll capture heap traces and kernel logs.
Carla SRE: Opening a targeted incident investigation ticket and linking this thread. Suggest we also snapshot the canary nodes for postmortem.
Ben (oncall): Who will own follow-up? Dmitri for RCA, Carla for incident write-up and mitigation playbook, Eva/Fred for customer updates. I'll remain the responder for 1hr then hand off to next oncall.
PagerBot: Paging next oncall: @alice_oncall in 60m for handoff.
DeployBot: NOTE: removed canary routing for meridian-labs to reserved-reserve-12 as part of pin rollback. Config snippet applied:
```
route:
  tenant: meridian-labs
  pinned_artifact: model-serving:2026-03-15-v1.3.6
  pool: reserved-reserve-12
```
Carla SRE: Added temporary alert mute for meridian-labs noise alarm to avoid alert fatigue while we stabilize. (will revert after 2h)
Dmitri (eng-platform): Collected traces and heap profiles: uploading to the incident ticket. Attaching lightweight reproduction script for ops to run in staging.
Ben (oncall): Good work. Next steps: 1) Keep pin in place, 2) Snapshot canary nodes + logs, 3) Run reproducer in staging against v1.3.7, 4) Draft rollback criteria for global canary rollback if we see broader spread.
Eva (CS): Customer acknowledged: "Thanks — traffic restored. We'll watch and let you know if anything else pops up."
Fred (AM): Marking customer priority P0 and posting to the account slack channel.
Carla SRE: Filing a post-incident task: add automatic rollback policy when canary 5xx > 3% sustained for 5m for dedicated pools with pinned tenants.
Ben (oncall): Handing responder baton to @alice_oncall in 50m. I'll leave notes in the ticket with commands run and current state.
PagerBot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigation applied (tenant pinback). Impact: meridian-labs restored to baseline. Investigation assigned.
DeployBot: LOG: `nginx: upstream timed out (504) at 2026-03-15T15:07:12Z` (sample)
Dmitri (eng-platform): Will follow up with a patch candidate to v1.3.7 if we can pinpoint the regression. If not safe, we'll recommend freezing canary and rolling a hotfix or revert.
Ben (oncall): Closing active page. Moving to monitoring / RCA. If anyone sees re-escalation, reactivate. :thumbsup:
